claim: No 2-star Michelin restaurants exist in San Diego; Addison earned 1 star in 2019, 2 stars in 2020, and 3 stars in 2021 and held them through 2025
quote: Addison (San Diego) — Stars: 3 Michelin stars (as of 2025). Star Progression: Earned 1 star in 2019, advanced to 2 stars in 2020, and reached the highest 3-star designation by 2021

claim: San Diego has five Michelin-starred establishments in total, with Addison holding the only 3-star designation in Southern California
quote: San Diego now boasts five establishments with Michelin stars, including one that has earned Michelin's top global honor of three stars

claim: Addison offers a 10-course tasting menu at $395/person and a Champagne Lounge experience at $198/person with optional champagne pairing at $175
quote: ten-course tasting menu... $395 per person. Champagne Lounge experience... $198 per guest, with optional Champagne pairings for $175

claim: Addison closed for a 7-week renovation on April 1, 2026 and reopened May 19, 2026 with a refreshed dining room and new champagne lounge
quote: Addison Plans Seven-Week Closure For Renovation... San Diego's three Michelin-star Addison will soon close for a nearly two months refresh tied to its 20th anniversary

claim: The renovation aimed to modernize without disturbing the Spanish Colonial Revival bones of the space; Chef Bradley also aims to earn 3 stars at a second restaurant
quote: modernize without disturbing the Spanish Colonial Revival bones of the space... Because he dared to do it — referring to Thomas Keller earning three stars at two restaurants

claim: The Addison dining experience lasts 3+ hours with synchronized plating, widely spaced tables, and optional premium upgrades including Wagyu
quote: well-spaced seating and soft lighting... tables are more spaciously arranged than typical fine-dining establishments... anticipating our needs before we even realized them ourselves

claim: A 2025 Addison dinner was priced at $385/person for 10 courses; Cantonese quail was cited as a standout dish
quote: $385 per person for a 10-course experience available Tuesday through Saturday, with the final seating at 8:30 PM... possibly the best quail I've ever eaten

claim: Valle is oceanfront at the Mission Pacific Hotel in Oceanside, specializing in contemporary Mexican cuisine with Baja California wines
quote: Valle is situated oceanfront in Oceanside, California, offering views of the iconic Oceanside Pier. The restaurant combines authentic and approachable dining

claim: Valle's main seasonal tasting menu is $220++ per person with a Mexican Wine Pairing option at +$170; a concise tasting is available at $140++
quote: Valle's main seasonal tasting menu is $220++ (per person), with wine pairing options including Mexican Wine Pairing at +$170

claim: Chef Roberto Alcocer has over 25 years of experience across Baja, France, and Spain and was a 2025 James Beard Award semifinalist
quote: Chef Roberto Alcocer... 2025 James Beard Award semifinalist. With more than 25 years of experience in acclaimed kitchens across Baja, California, France, and Spain

claim: Lilo is a 22-seat tasting menu restaurant in a converted boogie board factory; the 12-course menu spotlights local spot prawns, California abalone, and 28-day dry-aged beef
quote: Lilo is an intimate 22-seat tasting menu restaurant housed in a converted boogie board factory... locally caught spot prawns... California abalone... 28-day dry-aged beef

claim: Lilo's pairings: traditional $190, Champagne $290, non-alcoholic $110, hybrid $165
quote: four pairing options: traditional ($190), Champagne ($290), non-alcoholic ($110), and a hybrid ($165), and the meal typically runs just under three hours

claim: Lilo earned its Michelin star within 10 weeks of opening in April 2025
quote: Lilo restaurant in Carlsbad earns Michelin star in first 10 weeks of business

claim: Chef Eric Bost trained with Guy Savoy and has worked in prestigious kitchens across Singapore, New York, and Paris
quote: Chef Eric Bost trained with culinary masters including Guy Savoy. He's worked in prestigious kitchens all over the world, from Singapore to New York City to Paris

claim: Jeune et Jolie's 4-course prix fixe is priced at $105–$120 per person; a walk-in bar menu (Le Menu du Bar) is also available
quote: 4-course menu offered at $105 per person... Most diners opt for the perfectly pitched prix fixe, though à la carte offers many of the same dishes for those looking for a quick snack at the bar

claim: Soichi is a traditional omakase counter in University Heights where diners interact with chef Soichi Kadoya; ingredients sourced directly from Japan
quote: Soichi is an intimate Japanese restaurant... unforgettable omakase dining experience... culinary experience features a carefully curated omakase menu showcasing the freshest ingredients sourced directly from Japan
